items.evidence: The first section after the title is "## The bottom line", and it holds, in order, "**1. What FRUS answers directly.** FRUS answers both halves of the question, and the answer changes several times...", "**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.** *Where the printed documents came from:* ...", and "**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.** (a) *A complete census of decisions.* ...", followed by "**Scope.**" and "## Decisions this needs from you"; "## Findings" and its first finding ("### 1. Before Wilson...") come only after all three parts.

Every number names its set and base: "This rests on 43 documents, read whole, out of a scope of about 2,450 documents in 54 volumes"; "more than nine in ten of the source citations in the scope are numbers in the State Department's Central Decimal File"; "fewer than one document in twenty carries such a citation"; "across the 17 Latin American volumes of 1951–1988 finds about 110 documents in 15 of them"; "present in 552 of the 553 volumes"; "The Mexican chapters are almost a third of the scope"; "I retrieved 51 documents whole, read 45 of them, and cite 43; every quotation here (24 passages)". No percent sign appears in the file. The weakest figure is "(28 documents in 18 volumes)" for the Estrada Doctrine, which names what is counted but not whether the 553 volumes or the 54 scope volumes were searched; it is still a count of a named set, not a bare percentage or a baseless figure.

43 distinct documents are linked, and every frus…/d… string in the file sits inside a history.state.gov URL (a scan found none outside one); each document has at least one printed-edition citation, e.g. "(Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1907, Part II, Document 22, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1907p2/d22)" and "(Foreign Relations of the United States, Diplomatic Papers, 1932, The American Republics, Volume V, Document 618, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1932v05/d618)". Repeat mentions use continuation forms — "(1930, Volume I, Document 375, https://...frus1930v01/d375)", "(Document 136, https://...frus1952-54v04/d136)" directly after a same-volume citation, and the excerpt bullets' "(1913, Document 7)" — and one repeat, "(1936, Volume V, Document 112)" in Finding 4, carries no link, but that document is cited in full with its link in bottom line 1. Nothing is cited by a bare id pair or by title alone. The collection holds all 43 cited documents and all 24 quoted passages as excerpts, as the overview claims.

Part 3(a) is stated as runs with terms, volumes and controls: "I searched the editors' tables of contents in all 553 volumes for chapters naming recognition: the Latin American ones run from 1895 to 1950 and stop there, and before 1895 no chapter title names recognition of a Latin American government. A search for \"recognize/recognition\" near \"government\" with \"de facto\", \"revolution\" or \"provisional\" finds about six hundred unchaptered candidates in 58 volumes before 1895 (I read two, on Díaz), and a search pairing \"recognize/recognition\" with \"junta\", \"coup\", \"new government\", \"de facto\", \"provisional government\", \"military government\" or \"military regime\" across the 17 Latin American volumes of 1951–1988 finds about 110 documents in 15 of them; the phrase \"Department of State\" (present in 552 of the 553 volumes) and an impossible string (found nowhere) were run as controls." Part 3(b): "A search for \"Legal Adviser\" within thirty words of \"recognize/recognition\" in the 54 scope volumes finds four documents". Part 3(d) measures "by force" against its rate "anywhere in FRUS". The one residual assertion is 3(c)'s "the foreign ministries' own deliberations are not in FRUS and the bundled data offers no shelf for them", beside an Estrada count whose searched volumes are not named.

No SQL keyword, no table or column name, no underscore, no percent sign and no file path appears anywhere in the file; all 43 frus…/d… strings sit inside history.state.gov URLs (a scan found none outside one). The only identifiers are archival ones — "Record Group 59", "Lot 62 D 1, entry A1 1583E–F, NARA 2838992, 1948–1961, partly restricted", "8xx.00", "POL 16", "microfilm M862, series 654171" — and the index is named only in prose ("a read-only copy of the FRUS Explorer index (all 553 volumes) and the published TEI text", "the app's bundled NARA indexes").

judge:r6.rankingReason: r7 first: the widest span (1865–1980) and the most evidence (49 documents cited, every citation numbered and linked), the "what did it ask" half answered with counted terms over named bases (elections 106 of 1,131; consultation 37 of 186 in 1943–51; communism 19 of 81 in 1952–60), the Legal Adviser's 1939 rule and the 1907 convention text, and its one zero (1981–88) carrying its own control — at the cost of 500-word paragraphs, two continuation citations ("Document 109", "Document 159") that read as Volume XII when their links go to the Microfiche Supplement, and "the fifty-eight documents above" when 49 are cited. r6 second: the clearest to read — six short findings with bulleted, checked quotations, explicit defaults in the decisions, both controls named, the fullest shelf detail (entry numbers, date spans and access status for each lot) and a collection that matches it exactly (43 documents, 24 excerpts, six sections) — but thinner where the editors stop chaptering: eleven post-1950 markers, nothing after 1973, two of about six hundred pre-1895 candidates read, and the Estrada count's searched volumes unnamed. r3 last: 38 documents in 25 volumes with 18 of its 21 linked citations lacking a document number (two give only series and volume), an off-scope 1973 Afghanistan instruction, a Hughes briefing read to 9,500 of 33,346 characters, and a "cases not read" list where a measured zero belongs.

items.evidence: memo §0: "Coverage query, first call of the session: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT volume_id), COUNT(*), SUM(is_front_matter), SUM(is_editorial_note) FROM document_cache; → 553|321749|1103|8481"; queries.log line 1 is that command. memo §0: "All 553 volumes of the series are in this copy ... Every count here is conditional on this 553-volume index." Overview, Scope: "All 553 FRUS volumes are in the index used, so these figures describe the whole published series as indexed, not a partial library."

Memo cites every document as a pair (§4 table: "Q1 | frus1877/d222", "Q15 | frus1952-54v04/d327"); cited.tsv is 43 rows of `F# volume_id document_id`; the collection's entries carry volumeId/documentId. The overview's reader-facing citations carry the pair inside each permalink ("https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1877/d222"), never a title alone.

No rowid is reported anywhere; raw/read_ledger.tsv, raw/cited_meta.tsv, raw/scope_all.tsv and every result list are keyed by the pair. The only rowid in any query is the FTS content join `JOIN document_cache dc ON dc.rowid=f.rowid`, which is the index's own linkage (schema: `content='document_cache', content_rowid='rowid'`); nothing carries a rowid between queries or into a file.

channels.py: "JOIN document_sources ds ON ds.volume_id=s.volume_id AND ds.document_id=s.document_id" and "JOIN external_citations ec ON ec.volume_id=s.volume_id AND ec.document_id=s.document_id"; gloss.py and raw/decades.txt join document_dates "ON dd.volume_id=s.volume_id AND dd.document_id=s.document_id"; scope.py line 99 joins document_dates on both keys; the TEMP table s has `PRIMARY KEY(volume_id,document_id)`.

The overview opens with "## The bottom line" in three numbered parts: "**1. What FRUS answers directly.**" with documents cited (1877 d222, 1904 d228, 1913 d7, 1936 d112 by title, number and permalink); "**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.**" naming series by channel ("Where the printed documents came from: ... Central Decimal File (Record Group 59 ...)" / "What the editors cited without printing: ... Rubottom files ... NARA 2108779"); "**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.**" with the searches that established each gap ("I searched the editors' tables of contents in all 553 volumes", "A search for 'Legal Adviser' within thirty words of 'recognize/recognition' in the 54 scope volumes finds four documents").

score:r6.notes: All four named files are present (memo.md 373 lines, overview.md 61, queries.log 123, collection.fruscollection), plus the run's scripts, raw/ outputs (33 files, 51 saved documents) and quotes.json. Compliance 32/34 = 94.1%. Independent verification against the read-only copy and the bundled JSON: the coverage row, the 312,169 non-apparatus baseline, all seven M4 false-friend rows, the came-from (2,352; decimal 2,260; the lot list) and pointed-at (132 rows on 99 documents; anchor split; decimal top) counts, the decade numerators, the R1+R2 date span, the \"Department of State\" control (94,049 in 552), \"Estrada doctrine\" (28 in 18), \"legal advis\" 0 vs \"legal adviser\" 2,185, the 0-of-624 digitized ranges, the POL 16/POL 23-9 glosses, and the lot-to-NAID resolutions (64D199→602231; 59D573/61D279→2108779) all reproduce; all 24 quotations are exact substrings of body_text, the collection's 43 documents equal the overview's 43 cited pairs, and all 43 cited and 23 quoted documents appear in fetch.py lines in the log. Small discrepancies that touched no verdict: the memo says \"695 bundled series\" where series-facts-index.json's byNaId has 698 entries; 812.00 is 626 glossed against 628 came-from rows with that key (the gloss is date-gated, as the memo says). The two violations are narrow: O2 fails on one untraced quantitative claim (\"doubles the Central American material of the 1930s\"); P6 fails because several JSON-derived figures (0 of 624; roll NAID 19794147; no series-facts row for 302021; the POL labels; 11 of 695) have no on-disk output and one of them (11 of 695) has no log line, although the log is honest about the elision and every SQL-backed number shows its predicate. Judgement calls recorded in evidence: I2 treats the FTS content join on rowid as the index's linkage rather than an identifier; O1 treats history.state.gov permalinks as reader-facing citations rather than id pairs; S5 is obeyed on the scope check, with the 701 unfolded duplicate documents in the corpus baseline (0.2%) noted. E3 is not_applicable because cross_references was never queried beyond the schema listing.

Normalised segment check (lower-case, [^a-z0-9] dropped, split at …/.../[...]) against header||dateline||source_note||body_text of the memo's pair: 25/25 overview spans OK, 24/24 excerpts OK, 24/24 memo Q-table rows OK; citations beside each quotation resolve to the same pair (manifest titles checked for all 27 cited volumes; document_number equals the cited number for all 43). 0 fabrications, 0 mis-citations.

4. IDENTIFIERS — a recursive search of 13 bundled JSONs for each NAID string, then the series-facts legend decoded (statuses: 0 'Restricted - Fully', 1 'Unrestricted', 2 'Restricted - Partly', 3 'Restricted - Possibly'; creators from headings[]), lotFiles by lotNumber, lot-claimants, presidential-library-catalog, subject-numeric and decimal-class labels, digitized-ranges (0 of 624 ranges in 71x–73x/81x–83x; classes present are 763, 133, 131). 44 checked, 44 confirmed; the two ¶3 Legal Adviser lots and the pre-1906 'no file citation' claim (79 documents, 0 source rows) also confirmed.
